races.name: Royal Ascot Trials At Naas Rated Race

runners_data.name: Shaftesbury Avenue
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits under Ryan Moore, cheekpieces helped last time but 48 days off is notable
runners_data.comment: Both starts on heavy, pedigree suggests quick ground will be a huge plus, picked by Moore
runners_data.spotlight: Both runs over 1m on heavy ground; 5l third of 23 on debut at the Curragh behind Victory Tip; got his head in front next time at Navan in first-time cheekpieces (retained) and runner up has won since; pedigree suggests there could be lots more to come on quicker ground and he's the choice of Ryan Moore; big player.

runners_data.name: Victory Tip
runners_data.note: Beat Shaftesbury Avenue on debut but disappointed over further last time, needs to prove 1m2f failure was distance-related
runners_data.comment: Beat Shaftesbury Avenue on debut, last in Ballysax Stakes, must rebound back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Had Shaftesbury Avenue 5l behind when springing a 16-1 surprise on debut at the Curragh in March (1m, heavy); weakened quickly when last to finish upped to 1m2f in the Group 3 Ballysax at Leopardstown; needs to rebound now dropped back to 1m.

runners_data.name: Accredited
runners_data.note: Hold-up style may struggle with small field pace, but won well here on seasonal return for in-form O'Brien yard
runners_data.comment: 7f win on soft here on seasonal return, rated 97, deserted by Moore but can't discount
runners_data.spotlight: One of three for top yard; promise when a 2.5l fourth on debut at Dundalk (7f) last October; off the mark on seasonal return in a 7f maiden here on soft in March and earned an official rating of 97; deserted by Moore upped in trip but rider's 5lb claim useful off top weight; can't discount.

runners_data.name: Latin America
runners_data.note: Strong recent form over further suggests well-handicapped, hold-up style needs strong gallop to be effective
runners_data.comment: Off the mark on second start at Navan (1m2f), drop back to 1m a query but in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Promising debut at the Curragh (1m2f, sft-hvy) in March when chasing home the 102 rated Shaihann; went one place better at Navan (1m2f, gd-yld) in April, winning a median auction maiden by 2.25l; the drop back to 1m is a query but there's plenty of speed on the dam side of his pedigree; in the mix.

runners_data.name: New Radical
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with upward form curve, trainer Jack Davison 0/8 in last 14 days is concerning statistical angle
runners_data.comment: Off the mark by a head at Bellewstown, form boosted, may be more to come; cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Decent effort when an 8.25l third of 12 on debut at Dundalk (1m) in February; got up late on soft ground at Bellewstown (1m) last month and the fourth from that race (beaten 13.5l) has won a maiden since; needs to improve again but that's not impossible; cheekpieces on.

runners_data.name: Port Ferdinand
runners_data.note: Another O'Brien hold-up type who needs luck in running, recent course winner but step up in class significant

runners_data.name: Bobby McGee
runners_data.note: In-form prominent runner with perfect record this season, Colin Keane booking suggests strong confidence from connections
runners_data.comment: Promise at two, 2-2 this season, C&D handicap win latest, another big step forward needed
runners_data.spotlight: Some promising efforts at two without winning; has made a flawless start to his 3yo career, winning a Gowran maiden (7f, soft) and a C&D handicap (good) off 83; now rated 88 and worth his place in this field but probably needs to take another big step forward.

races.paceDynamic: Shaftesbury Avenue and Victory Tip will likely contest the early pace given their prominent styles, with Bobby McGee and New Radical also capable of tracking close. The presence of multiple hold-up horses (Accredited, Latin America, Port Ferdinand) suggests the pace won't be frantic early, allowing the leaders to dictate terms. With only 7 runners over 1m on good ground, this sets up as a steadily-run affair that will turn into a sprint finish. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position handy and kick, as the hold-up horses may find insufficient pace to run at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady as expected with Shaftesbury Avenue controlling from the front
scenarios.body: The handy horses can save energy for a sustained kick while hold-up types struggle for galloping room in a small field. Victory Tip and Bobby McGee benefit most from tracking the favourite's pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses go too fast early or tie up in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Latin America and Accredited can use their class to sweep past tired leaders in the closing stages. Their stronger ratings suggest they have the ability to overcome tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Favourite Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Shaftesbury Avenue gets an uncontested lead and Ryan Moore judges the pace perfectly
scenarios.body: The class horse dictates throughout and kicks clear when it matters, using superior tactical speed. His recent form over the distance on heavy suggests good current condition.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If all the prominent horses go too conservatively and it becomes a messy sprint
scenarios.body: The race turns into a rough scramble where any horse can win depending on racing luck and position. Port Ferdinand's hold-up style could prove decisive if he gets the gaps.

watchPoints.text: Victory Tip's market position - if weak in betting suggests connections doubt he stays or handles conditions
How aggressively Shaftesbury Avenue goes early under Ryan Moore - could set race up for closers if too keen
Latin America's ability to get competitive position early - needs to be closer than usual in small field
Bobby McGee's weight advantage at 126lbs combined with current form could be underestimated by market
Port Ferdinand and Accredited fighting for same tactical ground late - one could compromise the other's chance

races.name: ALTO Equine Building Solutions Handicap

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 232-day break with strong Leopardstown form but needs everything to fall right from the back
runners_data.comment: Best runs last year came in cheekpieces but that headgear is not applied here
runners_data.spotlight: Best runs last year came in a valuable Leopardstown handicap (1m1f, good to firm) when second in first-time cheekpieces, and when a close sixth at the Curragh next time in the same headgear; form regressed when headgear left off in two runs afterwards and it doesn't appear here.

runners_data.name: Final Voyage
runners_data.note: Confirmed stayer who won at Cork last month but disappointed when dropped to 7f, needs the mile trip
runners_data.comment: Ended long losing sequence at Cork; didn't appreciate drop to 7f latest; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Ended a long losing sequence with a 10.5f Cork win last month under this rider (good to yielding) off 5lb lower; didn't appear to appreciate drop to 7f back at Cork last time when staying on for seventh (short head behind Dark Viper); others more likely.

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer wearing cheekpieces with nine runner-up finishes, solid each-way claims
runners_data.comment: 2-22 but runner-up nine times; decent return last time but Vega's Muse is number one
runners_data.spotlight: Just 2-22 but has taken the runner-up spot nine times; won on heavy at Leopardstown in October off 5lb lower; decent enough return at Cork (7f, soft) when a 6l sixth; Vega's Muse appears to be stable number one.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent current form with two recent placings, perfectly suited to track the leader
runners_data.comment: Winner on penultimate but struggled off revised mark latest; must resume progress
runners_data.spotlight: Navan maiden winner over 5f on soft in October; returned this term in fine form, runner-up at the Curragh over 6f before going one better at Leopardstown over 7f (yielding to soft); struggled off revised mark at Gowran last time; needs to resume progress.

runners_data.name: Fast Tara
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with tactical advantage but poor strike rate of 1-24 despite consistent placing record
runners_data.comment: Rallied for a close second last time; should go well again but this ground may not suit
runners_data.spotlight: Led, was headed, but then rallied for a 0.5l third of 16 at Limerick (1m, yielding); 1-24 strike rate is not a great return but has placed on many occasions; should go well again off 1lb higher, but this ground may not suit.

runners_data.name: Bella Isabella
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 246-day absence for powerful Weld stable, Group 3-placed last season
runners_data.comment: M'den winner ran a decent race in second h'cap in final start last term; needs more
runners_data.spotlight: Cork maiden winner (7f, good) last season went on to take third of eight in a Leopardstown Group 3 next time (7f, good); ran to her rating when seventh of 20 in a Leopardstown handicap on her final start last term (1m, good to yielding); needs a bit more.

runners_data.name: Vega's Muse
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won well at Leopardstown on seasonal return, ideally positioned to track Fast Tara
runners_data.comment: Easy winner on return but follow-up attempt perhaps came too quickly; not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: Added second turf win when keeping on well to comfortably land a 1m Leopardstown handicap on seasonal return (1m, good to yielding); follow-up attempt under a 7lb penalty perhaps came too quickly on softer ground; up 10lb compared to her win but not discounted.

runners_data.name: Far From Dandy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in career-best form with recent Dundalk wins, dangerous if getting clear run late
runners_data.comment: In fine form and ran a career best when runner-up at Doncaster; big chance
runners_data.spotlight: One of two for trainer; career-best form since November features two wins at Dundalk and a fourth-place finish in the Irish Lincolnshire; better again in the Spring Mile at Doncaster last time when a runner-up off 1lb lower (1m, good to soft); big chance with ground to suit.

runners_data.name: Jagged Edge
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced prominent runner returning from 245-day break, talented but ring-rusty concerns
runners_data.comment: Irish Cambridgeshire winner last season is lightly raced and runs well fresh
runners_data.spotlight: One of two for trainer; lightly-raced 4yo didn't race at two; won twice in a five-race career for Dermot Weld last season; won a 1m Cork maiden and the Irish Cambridgeshire at the Curragh (1m, good to yielding) off 3lb lower after a three-month absence; way below that in final start at the Curragh; runs well fresh, so not out of it on stable debut.

runners_data.name: Speckled Meadow
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up performer who won here in October, needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Four-time h'cap winner; out of depth on return; this more realistic but others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Added her fourth handicap win over 10.5f here in October off 63 (yielding); decent fourth in a higher grade next time at Leopardstown (1m4f, heavy) but disappointed at the Curragh on her final start of 2025; out of her depth on return at Cork; this more realistic but others preferred.

runners_data.name: Daler
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who broke maiden at Dundalk, better on turf but needs gaps to appear late
runners_data.comment: Just fair efforts since first win on AW in October; could go well back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Got first career win with a comfortable 1m Dundalk handicap success in October off 72; just fair efforts on AW since, but he has some decent turf form and could go well back on this surface.

runners_data.name: Senna's Girl
runners_data.note: Winless hold-up mare with decent recent form, wearing cheekpieces and tongue-tie for first time
runners_data.comment: 0-14 but has gone close; good runs last twice and not out of it
runners_data.spotlight: 0-14 but has gone close at times; good run from a wide draw in a 7f Leopardstown (yielding to soft) contest, staying on well; another positive effort when third in a Limerick maiden in this headgear latest (1m, yielding); slowly away that day so effort can be marked up; not out of it.

runners_data.name: Red Charlie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to turf after 493-day break win, may need race fitness
runners_data.comment: Returned from long absence to win at Curragh and almost followed up latest; player
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from a 493-day absence over 7f at the Curragh when comfortably winning a 23-runner contest (soft to heavy); almost followed up off 15lb higher back there next time, when hampered before finishing strongly to lose out by a head; up another 3lb, but he's thriving and a definite chance if handling this better ground and step up in trip.

races.paceDynamic: Fast Tara will be the sole confirmed early leader, likely joined by prominent runners Glory To Be, Vega's Muse, Jagged Edge and Red Charlie in the early positions. With only one dedicated front-runner, Fast Tara should get an uncontested lead and sustainable fractions over this mile trip on good ground. The majority of the field are hold-up horses including Booyea, Final Voyage, Dark Viper, Bella Isabella, Far From Dandy, Speckled Meadow, Daler and Senna's Girl, creating a large chasing pack that will need to find racing room in the straight. This pace scenario strongly favours prominent runners and the leader, as they avoid traffic problems and benefit from the controlled early tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Fast Tara gets soft early fractions and stays strong
scenarios.body: The lone pace-setter controls the race throughout and the prominent runners fill the placings ahead of the traffic-laden hold-up brigade. The sustainable tempo plays perfectly into the hands of those racing handy to the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Glory To Be or Vega's Muse improve past Fast Tara in the straight
scenarios.body: The early prominent horses benefit from ideal positioning as Fast Tara weakens, while the hold-up horses struggle for clear runs in a bunched finish. The tactical advantage of racing close to the pace proves decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Powers Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the back-markers gets a dream run through gaps late
scenarios.body: A strong-staying hold-up performer like Far From Dandy or Booyea finds the perfect split and powers home past tiring leaders. The good ground and strong pace sets up perfectly for a late charge from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic-Free Outsider Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the main fancies get hampered and a mid-priced runner finds daylight
scenarios.body: An unconsidered runner like Daler or Senna's Girl benefits from a trouble-free trip while the market leaders encounter interference. The chaotic finish allows an outsider to slip through unnoticed.

watchPoints.text: Fast Tara could get an armchair ride if no other horse wants to go forward early, creating difficult catching conditions
The large group of hold-up horses including Far From Dandy, Booyea and Final Voyage will create significant traffic problems in the straight
Glory To Be and Vega's Muse are both in excellent current form and perfectly positioned to track the lone leader
Bella Isabella returns from a long break for the shrewd Weld yard and could be well-handicapped off her current mark
Jagged Edge showed high-class form for Weld last season but the 245-day break raises fitness concerns for new connections

races.name: Coolmore Stud Blackbeard Race

runners_data.name: Pala Aurelia
runners_data.note: Lightly raced newcomer with unknown running style but strong connections suggest she could be anything on debut
runners_data.comment: St Mark's Basilica filly; 230,000gns 2yo is half-sister to five winners; check market
runners_data.spotlight: St Mark's Basilica filly; 62,000euros yearling was then purchased for 230,000gns as a 2yo; half-sister to five winners inc' Too Soon To Panic (1m/9.4f inc Listed; RPR 106), Wargrave (7f turf/1m2f snow, 102; 2m hurdle) and Ahandfulofsummers (1m1f; 98); dam 5f/6f winner (inc 2yo/Group 3; 106); interesting pedigree and worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs genuine pace to be effective and won well last time at the Curragh
runners_data.comment: Off the mark first time at the Curragh; different ground here but leading contender
runners_data.spotlight: Starman colt got off the mark at the first time of asking over 5f at the Curragh (soft) when 1.25l ahead of What A Girl Wants; ran through the line strongly and while he has different ground to contend with now, he is a half-brother to two fast-ground winners; leading contender.

runners_data.name: What A Girl Wants
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has shown consistent form and represents the same trainer as Your Song creating tactical intrigue
runners_data.comment: 1.25l behind Star Prospect on debut and 3lb better off now; 6l ahead of New Yorker latest
runners_data.spotlight: One of two for trainer; made a promising start when a 1.25l third behind Star Prospect at the Curragh last month (5f, soft); showed improvement to take second in a 5f Curragh Listed contest last time (4-7 fav' New Yorker 6l behind in third); 3lb better off with Star Prospect now compared to their initial meeting; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Cyclone Code
runners_data.note: Limited based on moderate debut effort and faces a significant class rise against these better-rated opponents
runners_data.comment: Moderate sixth on debut; he will get easier opportunities than this
runners_data.spotlight: Moderate debut at Roscommon when a 6.5l sixth of ten (7.5f, good), weakening late on; he will have easier opportunities to get off the mark than this.

runners_data.name: Your Song
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who disappointed last time but gets ideal scenario with no pace pressure here

runners_data.name: New Yorker
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from powerful stable who won on debut but failed to follow up when odds-on favourite last time
runners_data.comment: Debut AW winner disappointed as 4-7 fav' last time when What A Girl Wants was 6l in front
runners_data.spotlight: Justified 4-7 favouritism at Dundalk on debut in April, when 1.25l in front despite showing signs of greenness over 5f; disappointed when sent off the same odds in a Curragh Listed contest last time (5f, good), running keenly and jinking right late on to fade into third (6l behind What A Girl Wants); something to prove now but likely has more to give.

races.paceDynamic: Your Song will be the clear early leader with no genuine pace pressure in this small field, allowing her to dictate terms from the front. The prominent runners What A Girl Wants and New Yorker will track behind but neither has shown the pace to seriously challenge Your Song's early position. With Star Prospect preferring to come from off the pace and Pala Aurelia an unknown quantity, Your Song can control fractions and potentially steal this at generous odds. This race shape strongly favours front runners and those who can sit handy, as the lack of genuine pace pressure means the leader won't be softened up for closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Your Song gets an easy lead without pressure from the prominent runners
scenarios.body: Your Song can dictate comfortable fractions and has enough in hand to resist late challenges. The lack of early pace allows her to conserve energy for the crucial final furlong where her stamina advantage tells.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Tells Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuine enough to set up the race for the better horses
scenarios.body: Star Prospect and Pala Aurelia can use their superior ratings to overcome the tactical disadvantage. The class difference becomes decisive in the final 100 yards as the early pace takes its toll.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If What A Girl Wants or New Yorker can position perfectly behind Your Song
scenarios.body: The tracking horse gets the ideal trip behind the leader and has enough tactical speed to strike at the right moment. Recent form and race fitness prove crucial in a sustained drive to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Your Song goes too slow early and the field bunches up for a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed contest over the final 2 furlongs where any horse can win. Cyclone Code or another outsider could benefit from the chaos of a slowly-run race turning into a dash.

watchPoints.text: Your Song breaking slowly could ruin the entire pace scenario as she is the only natural front runner
Watch for any market support for Pala Aurelia as connections may know she is well above average
Star Prospect needs the pace to be genuine early - if Your Song goes too slowly he will struggle to make up ground
What A Girl Wants and Your Song share the same trainer which creates interesting tactical dynamics
New Yorker has Ryan Moore aboard and any confident ride could signal Ballydoyle expect improvement

runners_data.name: Mai Dahlia
runners_data.comment: Too Darn Hot filly, half-sister to useful Ameerat Jumaira, tongue tied, check market
runners_data.spotlight: Too Darn Hot filly; half-sister to winners Ameerat Jumaira (Group-placed 10.6f-1m4f inc AW; RPR 99) and Jujubella (1m2f-12.4f inc AW; 78); dam unraced half-sister to UAE 1m2f Group 1 winner North America; appealing pedigree, yard in form and worth a market check; tongue tied.

runners_data.name: Rebel Wave
runners_data.comment: E280,000 New Bay filly, dam 7f US dirt winner, could go well, market best guide
runners_data.spotlight: New Bay filly's price rose from 110,000gns as a yearling to E280,000 as a foal; half-sister to winners Spanish Phoenix (5f 2yo; RPR 100) and Confident Star (5.5f-7f inc 2yo/Spain; 95); dam US 7f dirt winner, half-sister to smart 7f-1m1f winner Bell Rock; could go well on debut; market can guide.

runners_data.name: Sydney Dollars
runners_data.comment: E40,000 Mehmas filly, dam 6.5f-7f winner, market can guide on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Mehmas filly; E31,000 foal, E40,000 yearling; half-sister to winners Orglandes (French/US 1m1f-12.5f inc Grade 3; RPR 98) and Pittsford (10.6f AW; 83); dam 6.7f-7.5f winner (inc 2yo/AW; 92), out of 7f 2yo Group 2 winner; market check advised.

runners_data.name: Solana Beach
runners_data.comment: Very pleasing debut at over 7f at Gowran (soft), 1m and quicker ground should suit, chance
runners_data.spotlight: No Nay Never filly sent off at 14-1 on debut at Gowran (7f, soft) last month but outran those odds; short of room, ran green but stayed on very nicely once the penny dropped for a 4l second; pedigree suggests quicker ground will suit, as should this longer trip; interesting.

runners_data.name: Elmakaya
runners_data.comment: Late gains from wide draw after slowish start on Leopardstown debut, don't write off
runners_data.spotlight: Wootton Bassett filly sent off at 7-1 on debut at Leopardstown (1m, gd-yld) last month and could only manage a 5.75l seventh; however, she was a step slow away from a wide draw and made some pleasing late gains and this Irish Oaks entry isn't one to write off here.

runners_data.name: Totally Puzzled
runners_data.comment: Tailed off on seasonal return at the Curragh, hood goes on, drops in trip, best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Sea The Moon filly; showed ability when midfield on debut last October at Navan (1m, yielding); tailed off on seasonal return over 1m2f (sft-hvy) at the Curragh; drops back in trip and hooded; best watched.

runners_data.name: Wedding
runners_data.comment: Out of the frame in maidens at Gowran (1m) and Leopardstown (1m2f), cheekpieces tried
runners_data.spotlight: Expensively bought No Nay Never filly has finished out of the frame in maidens at Gowran (1m, soft) and Leopardstown (1m2f, good) on latest; drops back in trip now; Ryan Moore rides for the first time; new cheekpieces need to spark improvement.

races.name: Owenstown Stud Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Greek Mythology
runners_data.note: Front runner improving with each start but 39 days off and facing much stronger opposition than previous wins
runners_data.comment: Won AW debut in Dec'; okay run on return and could step forward on this better ground
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 7f Dundalk median auction race on debut in December; 3.25l second in a four-runner Gowran rated race on his return (7f, soft) last month; could step forward on this quicker ground.

runners_data.name: Rahmi
runners_data.note: Hold-up merchant with proven C&D form and class edge, 50 days freshness could be ideal for big effort
runners_data.comment: Three-time h'cap winner was disappointing on return; Tashakour looks stable's main hope
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time h'cap winner, including over C&D in final 2024 start; ran just three times last season; produced a smart display to win a 7f premier handicap at the Irish Champions meeting; towards rear throughout on comeback in a 7f Curragh Listed contest (soft to heavy); may be better suited by this ground but Tashakour looks like the yard's main hope.

runners_data.name: Expanded
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Ryan Moore booking suggesting confidence, recent 2nd shows he's in good heart

runners_data.name: King Cuan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace to be effective, 20 days perfect spacing for peak effort
runners_data.comment: Built on decent seasonal return when running on over 5f here last time; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time winner at 6f-7f; won just once last season when landing a three-runner auction race at Fairyhouse (6f, good); subsequently placed in Listed and Group 3 company; built on decent Cork return when running on well for fourth over 5f here last time, from disadvantageous side of the track; this trip suits better and not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Chantez
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 259-day break, Listed winner but long absence is major concern
runners_data.comment: Listed 2yo winner was unable to bag a Gr.3 in four runs last term; drops in grade now
runners_data.spotlight: Listed winner at Leopardstown as a 2yo; best of four Group 3 runs last season was when third at Leopardstown in July (7f, good to firm); drops in grade but this looks hard all the same.

runners_data.name: Native Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose visor addition transformed him, British raider with strong recent C&D-type form
runners_data.comment: British raider was a good second in a Gr.3 on return; entitled to improve and top rated
runners_data.spotlight: British raider rediscovered his best when a visor was added last June, winning three handicaps from five starts, the last being the valuable Challenge Cup (7f, soft) at Ascot; ran right up to form on his stakes debut in a Saint-Cloud Group 3 (1m, soft) for seasonal return when a close runner-up; entitled to improve for that and top rated.

runners_data.name: Wannabe Royal
runners_data.note: Front runner whose poor recent 6f form suggests 7f is minimum trip requirement
runners_data.comment: Maiden winner for Joseph O'Brien was poor at Cork; others more likely
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden winner over 7f for Joseph O'Brien on soft; ran well over that trip at the Curragh on seasonal/stable debut; poor over 6f at Cork last time; others more likely, especially on this ground.

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from Brazilian handler, recent all-weather form needs to translate to turf

runners_data.name: East Hampton
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran career-best in Group 2 last time, 50-day break since that breakthrough effort
runners_data.comment: Encouraging second on return but runs well fresh, so might not be boundless improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win last season came in the C&D Madrid handicap; ran a career best when a close second in the Curragh Group 2 Minstrel Stakes (7f, good to yielding) behind subsequent Group 1 winner Diego Velazquez; highly encouraging second in a Curragh Listed contest on return (7f, soft to heavy); however, he runs well fresh so there might not be boundless improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Tashakour
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping back from 1m success, 3yo improving rapidly with only 23 days since last win
runners_data.comment: Cork m'den winner last time has a bit to find in this company
runners_data.spotlight: Good second in a Navan maiden on seasonal return (1m, heavy); showed the benefit of that run when successful at Cork last time (1m, good to yielding); a bit to find in this company.

runners_data.name: Greydreambeliever
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making stable debut for O'Brien after British purchase, 25 days perfect preparation time
runners_data.comment: Useful British form and positive h'cap runs for new yard but this is a tall task
runners_data.spotlight: Some useful form in Britain for Karl Burke before being bought by current connections for 30,000gns; made a good stable debut when a runner-up in a Gowran handicap and improved when filling the same spot dropped to 7f back there next time; those runs were on soft, while her British form is on good, so could improve, but this is a tall task; Greek Mythology is stable first-string.

races.paceDynamic: Greek Mythology and Wannabe Royal will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front runners likely to set an honest gallop from the start. Expanded and Chantez should sit prominent behind the leaders, while the strong contingent of hold-up horses (Rahmi, Native Warrior, King Cuan, East Hampton, Tashakour, Greydreambeliever) will be positioned further back. The dual pace angle creates a solid tempo that should set up a strong finish, with the race likely to develop into a sprint from the 2f pole. This honest pace strongly favours the hold-up merchants and prominent racers with tactical speed over the front runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuine and both leaders tire
scenarios.body: The strong group of closers will have perfect conditions to unleash their finishing kicks in the final 2f. Rahmi's class and Native Warrior's recent visor form make them particularly dangerous from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Expanded or Chantez can secure the ideal pitch behind the leaders
scenarios.body: These horses can avoid the early battle while staying close enough to pounce when the pace kicks in. Expanded's Ballydoyle polish and recent run gives him the edge in this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace setters can establish a clear advantage and kick clear
scenarios.body: Greek Mythology's improving profile could see him dominate from the front if Wannabe Royal folds early. The 3yo would need to show significant improvement to hold off the closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset from Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the race becomes tactical early
scenarios.body: Tashakour's recent winning form at longer trips or Greydreambeliever's stable debut promise could catch the fancied runners napping. A messy pace would open the door for progressive types.

watchPoints.text: Greek Mythology and Wannabe Royal must be monitored early - if both go hard, they create perfect setup for closers
Chantez returning from 259-day absence faces fitness concerns despite Listed-winning ability
Native Warrior's visor retention is crucial given how much it transformed his form last season
Tashakour dropping back from mile success could struggle if pace isn't strong enough for his closing kick
Expanded's market support will indicate Ballydoyle confidence in his chances against this Listed field

races.name: Coolmore Stud Irish EBF Fillies Sprint Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Controlla
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced unknown with strong breeding but David Egan booking suggests connections expect improvement from this talented filly.
runners_data.comment: 160,000gns Night Of Thunder filly, related to useful winners, pitched in at the deep end
runners_data.spotlight: One of two for stable; Night Of Thunder filly; 160,000gns yearling; closely related to 8.6f AW 2yo/1m turf winner Khaloosy (RPR 114), half-sister to winners Moqtarreb (1m inc Listed; 109) and Zaajel (7f AW 2yo; 76); unplaced dam from family of Nathaniel; pitched in at the deep end on debut but yard's juveniles always respected.

runners_data.name: Victorious
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Ryan Moore aboard who showed smart acceleration at this C&D, perfectly positioned to exploit any pace collapse.
runners_data.comment: Impressive win on debut over C&D, from excellent family, should improve, big chance
runners_data.spotlight: Wootton Bassett filly from an excellent family made a winning start in a C&D maiden, displaying a smart turn of foot to beat Aedhmar (who was only a neck behind Velozee on her previous start at Cork) by 1.75l; yard's runners often improve plenty for their first runs and she looks an exciting prospect; big chance.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: Natural leader who has won both starts impressively, stepping up significantly in class but W J Lee retains the ride.
runners_data.comment: 2-2, impressive 5f listed win latest, bred to get 6f, sets the standard for red hot yard
runners_data.spotlight: Sioux Nation filly is 2-2; scored by a short head on soft at Cork on debut (5f); impressive display in four runner listed race at the Curragh latest (5f, good), after which the Albany Stakes was nominated as a possible target; bred to get 6f and sets the standard; yard in red hot form.

runners_data.name: Maria Quiteria
runners_data.note: Front-running type returning after 51-day break having won decisively at Dundalk, the freshness factor could be crucial.
runners_data.comment: Justified skinny odds on debut at Dundalk, should handle turf but this demands a lot more
runners_data.spotlight: Churchill filly justified skinny odds to win a five runner 5f Dundalk maiden decisively on debut in March; should stay 6f and handle quick ground on breeding but that form has taken some knocks and this demands a whole lot more.

runners_data.name: Vollering
runners_data.note: British raider and confirmed front runner under Hollie Doyle who dominated at Redcar but faces much stronger opposition here.
runners_data.comment: Powered clear late on to win on debut over 5f at Redcar, should get 6f, no forlorn hope
runners_data.spotlight: British raider; Sioux Nation filly displayed plenty of speed and ran on strongly in the final furlong to win a Redcar novice by 2.5l on debut (5f, gd-fm); the manner of that win and her pedigree suggests that 6f should pose no problems; looks well worth a go at this level and is no forlorn hope.

runners_data.name: Dancing Destiny
runners_data.note: Prominent racer on quick 6-day turnaround after 8f debut success, may struggle with this significant trip reduction.
runners_data.comment: Debut win over 7.5f at Roscommon, not sure this drop back to 6f will suit
runners_data.spotlight: Magna Grecia filly got off the mark on debut at Roscommon (7.5f, good) six days ago; didn't shape like she was crying out for a drop back in trip that day and her dam was best over 1m2f-1m4f; may be vulnerable to speedier rivals at this distance.

races.paceDynamic: Velozee and Vollering are both confirmed front runners who will contest the early pace from the gates, ensuring an honest gallop throughout. With just six runners, the prominent types Victorious, Maria Quiteria and Dancing Destiny will sit close behind the leaders, while the lightly-raced Controlla represents an unknown quantity tactically. The small field and two speed horses up front will create a searching test that should suit those with proven pace and tactical speed. This race shape strongly favours the front runners and prominent racers who can travel well early and have the class to sustain their effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Velozee or Vollering gets first run and the pace isn't suicidal
scenarios.body: The leader will have every chance to dictate terms and kick clear, with the small field unable to apply sustained pressure. Either speed horse can exploit their natural pace advantage and superior race experience over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders engage in a pace duel and compromise each other
scenarios.body: Victorious or Maria Quiteria can sit the perfect trip behind the battling leaders and pounce late. The class edge of Victorious or the fresh legs of Maria Quiteria after 51 days off can prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Controlla Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the unknown tactical setup of Controlla allows perfect positioning
scenarios.body: The lightly-raced Night Of Thunder filly could have significant untapped ability and benefit from racing off a pace that may be too strong. Her breeding suggests she'll handle this step up in class if allowed to settle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dancing Destiny Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the 8f debut winner shows more pace than expected stepping back in trip
scenarios.body: Despite not looking desperate for this shorter distance, her recent Roscommon win could have been a confidence booster. The quick turnaround of just 6 days may catch rivals cold if she's improved dramatically.

watchPoints.text: Velozee and Vollering must be monitored closely early to see if they engage in a pace duel that could compromise both chances.
Controlla's market moves will be telling given her lightly-raced profile and the David Egan jockey booking for this step up in class.
Maria Quiteria's sharpness after 51 days off needs assessing in the preliminaries, as freshness could be key or concerning.
Dancing Destiny's ability to show early pace on this quick turnaround will determine if the trip drop is workable.
Victorious needs the two leaders to go too fast early to set up her prominent running style perfectly.

races.name: Goffs Lacken Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Charles Darwin
runners_data.note: Front-running style faces strong pace pressure from two other confirmed leaders, though Ryan Moore's tactical nous could prove crucial
runners_data.comment: Last season's Norfolk Stakes winner was workmanlike on return but improvement likely
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten on debut at Cork before going the rest of the season unbeaten; landed a Navan maiden (6f, soft), a four-runner conditions event here (5f, good) and ultimately the Norfolk Stakes at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm); workmanlike when justifying short odds at Navan on seasonal return (6f, good to yielding) and there is likely improvement to come; holds Group 1 entries for Ascot.

runners_data.name: Havana Anna
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 198-day layoff with solid Group-level form, perfectly positioned to track the pace battle
runners_data.comment: Listed winner/Group 1 placed is top-rated and unpenalised but lacks a run
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden and Listed winner over 5f; beaten only a nose in a Group 3 over the minimum trip at Longchamp, though produced her best effort when chasing home True Love in the 6f Group 1 Cheveley Park; failed to cope with the challenge of the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint; appealing given her top-rating and she's unpenalised but lacks a run.

runners_data.name: Kindergarten
runners_data.note: Lead-seeking runner lacks experience against this grade, likely to get caught up in early speed duel
runners_data.comment: Plausible improvement to come over 1.75l defeat behind Charles Darwin on just second start
runners_data.spotlight: Winner of her sole start last year at Navan (6f, yielding); disputing second in a Navan Listed contest before fading late into fourth (6f, good to yielding); plausible improvement to come from that first run back and was just 1.75l behind the winner Charles Darwin, although worse off at the weights now.

runners_data.name: Josh's Joy
runners_data.note: Prominent style gives tactical options though moderate ability means needs everything to fall right
runners_data.comment: Won her m'den at the fourth attempt last season; okay return but this is a big ask
runners_data.spotlight: Positive efforts in maidens before landing a Naas contest at the fourth attempt (6f, yielding); okay return in a Curragh handicap last time when a 4l seventh (6f, soft to heavy); this is a big ask.

runners_data.name: Royal Bay Cen
runners_data.note: Front-runner with impressive Irish debut win but faces immediate pace pressure from Charles Darwin and Kindergarten
runners_data.comment: Mighty impressive Irish/stable debut in a Cork Listed race; big chance if handling ground
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 6f French winner at two; good efforts in a pair of Group 3s before signing off her French career with an underwhelming Group 2 start; mightily impressive Irish/stable debut at Cork (5.5f, soft) when pulverising seven rivals by 9l; big chance if building on that on this better ground.

runners_data.name: Tahcawin
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist perfectly suited to expected strong pace, recent 8-day turnaround keeps him sharp

runners_data.name: Chicago Call
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up style ideally suited to race shape, 22 days since last run provides freshness edge
runners_data.comment: Improved over moderate seasonal return when 3l behind at Navan latest; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 6f Fairyhouse maiden over this trip last July (good); best form when just denied in a Listed event at the same track in September (6f, yielding); improved over moderate seasonal return at Cork when a 3l sixth at Navan last time (6f, good to yielding); others preferred.

runners_data.name: Oh Cecelia
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with headgear fitted, 14-day gap since last run keeps her competitive
runners_data.comment: Beaten 9.5l by Royal Bay Cen in a Cork Listed race last time; a lot to find
runners_data.spotlight: Cork maiden winner (5f, good) for Jack Davison last year; made a winning stable debut in a Naas handicap in March (5f, soft) and added another victory in a Cork rated contest (5f, soft); beaten 9.5l by Royal Bay Cen in a Cork Listed race last time (5.5f, soft); a lot to find.

races.paceDynamic: Charles Darwin, Royal Bay Cen, and Kindergarten will create a fierce early battle with all three confirmed front-runners forcing a strong gallop from the gates. This sustained pace will test stamina reserves over 6f on good turf, with the leaders likely to engage from the 4f pole onwards. The relentless tempo will set up tactical opportunities for closers like Tahcawin and Chicago Call to sweep up tired leaders in the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can conserve energy and produce late kicks against stamina-sapped pace-setters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners engage in a speed duel through halfway
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will drain Charles Darwin, Royal Bay Cen and Kindergarten, allowing patient closers to exploit their finishing kicks. Hold-up specialists with tactical pace will prove superior as leaders hit the wall in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter can dictate terms without severe early pressure
scenarios.body: Charles Darwin or Royal Bay Cen could steal crucial lengths by avoiding the worst of the speed battle, maintaining enough reserves to repel late challenges. The class leader gets first run while others are still winding up their finishing efforts.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate allowing stalkers to travel comfortably
scenarios.body: Havana Anna and Josh's Joy can sit perfectly positioned behind the leaders, avoiding the speed battle while maintaining striking distance. They get the best of both worlds with tactical position and fresh finishing power over the final 2f.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders go suicidally fast from the outset
scenarios.body: The entire front rank will compound and stop dramatically, creating a sprint finish from deep in the field. Even moderate finishers will have winning chances as the race falls apart completely in front of them.

watchPoints.text: Charles Darwin and Royal Bay Cen engaging in early speed battle could compromise both their finishing kicks
Havana Anna returning from 198-day absence may need the run despite her high-class form
Kindergarten attempting to lead against superior pace-setters could see her drop away tamely
Tahcawin and Chicago Call getting clean runs from the back as the expected pace scenario unfolds
Oh Cecelia wearing headgear for first time suggesting connections expect improved effort

races.name: Sole Power Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Mission Central
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with top jockey aboard but faces traffic dangers in crowded position
runners_data.comment: Ready Listed C&D winner on seasonal return and big chance of following up under penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Won three of his six starts as a juvenile, including a Group 3 at the Curragh (6f, good to yielding) and a valuable conditions race at Ascot (6f, good); struggled when dropped to 5f at the Breeders' Cup on final start; ran out a ready winner of a C&D Listed contest on seasonal return to mark his first victory over the minimum trip; carries a penalty but big chance of following up.

runners_data.name: Moss Tucker
runners_data.note: Returning from long layoff as former Group 1 winner, prominent style adds to congestion concerns
runners_data.comment: Gr.1 winner in 2014 missed all of last season; some promise in his return here last time
runners_data.spotlight: Former Flying Five winner reached a peak rating of 114 before losing his form in the latter half of 2024; missed all of last season; return in a C&D Listed contest last time was not totally devoid of promise when 4.75l behind Mission Central; may build on that.

runners_data.name: Keke
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits this pace scenario, career-high mark but proven at this level
runners_data.comment: Added seventh win when winning h'cap here last time; needs to improve again
runners_data.spotlight: Seven wins over 5f and 6f generally on good ground; won off 97 in a 6f handicap here last time (good); his mark of 104 is a career high but he will need to improve again now entering stakes company.

runners_data.name: Kerdos
runners_data.note: New yard debut for former Group 2 winner, hold-up style could benefit from strong pace
runners_data.comment: Listed and Gr.2 winner was a 2.75l sixth behind Mission Central last time over C&D
runners_data.spotlight: Classy sprinter for Clive Cox and won a Listed and a Group 2 for that yard; decent run on debut for this yard at Dundalk before disappointing in Cork Listed race next time on soft; much better over C&D last time when a 2.75l sixth behind Mission Central.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who'll add to the traffic problems, 3yo getting weight allowance
runners_data.comment: Won a m'den and two Listed races last season but a disappointing seventh at Cork last time
runners_data.spotlight: Winner of a 6f Curragh maiden but seemed better suited to 5f as the season progressed; won two Listed races at the Curragh and Dundalk over the minimum trip; narrowly lost out to longer priced stablemate on seasonal debut at Dundalk; 5-4 favourite at Cork (5.5f, soft) last time when a disappointing seventh of eight; this ground may suit better but others preferred.

runners_data.name: Lady Iman
runners_data.note: Long absence since October could blunt sharpness, prominent style faces navigation issues
runners_data.comment: Impressive CV in opening runs last term; big player on ratings but lacks a run
runners_data.spotlight: Amassed an impressive CV in her opening runs last season; won her AW maiden before landing a 5f Curragh Listed contest, and a Naas Group 3; failed to justify 8-15 odds in a Curragh Group 2 before resuming progress with a Molecomb Stakes victory at Goodwood; form tapered off in her final two Group runs; big player on ratings but lacks a run.

runners_data.name: Valiant Force
runners_data.note: Uncontested leader perfectly positioned to exploit this race shape, turf record poor though
runners_data.comment: Just 1-12 on turf and 7.5l behind Keke in a h'cap last time; others arrive in better form
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win on turf in the 2023 Norfolk Stakes; has won five conditions races at Dundalk since, the most recent a 4.25l win over 5f in February; well beaten at Lingfield, Newcastle and when 7.5l behind Keke in a 6f handicap here last time; others arrive in better form.

runners_data.name: Gazelle d'Or
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs clear runs, returning from disappointing Curragh effort
runners_data.comment: Not the clearest of runs when 12th of 15 in C&D Listed contest latest; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time winner at 5f-6f on good and yielding ground; not at best on Curragh return; didn't get the clearest of runs when 12th of 15 and 5.5l behind the winner Mission Central in a C&D Listed contest last time; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Black Forza
runners_data.note: Long layoff and hold-up style, former Group 2 winner with tactical advantage here
runners_data.comment: Gr.2 winner in 2024 ran okay on AW in final two runs; more needed here and lacks a run
runners_data.spotlight: Winner of a Goodwood Group 2 in 2024; sparingly raced last year, well beaten in a Curragh Group 3 (6f, good); some better efforts twice at Dundalk but more needed here and lacks a run.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner but form decline makes her vulnerable at this level
runners_data.comment: Three-time winner hasn't been at her best so far this season and this is tough
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time winner over this trip on varying ground types but hasn't been at her best so far this season and this looks too tough.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Prominent style adds to congestion, career-best last time but faces tougher task
runners_data.comment: 1-12 but some near misses inc' when 0.75l behind Mission Central here latest; chance
runners_data.spotlight: 1-12 on turf but has had a few near misses, including when beaten a short head in a 5f Curragh handicap (soft) on penultimate; ran a career best over C&D last time when 0.75l behind Mission Central; better off with that rival now; good chance with a repeat.

runners_data.name: Billie Be Quick
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose style suits but form figures suggest she's outclassed

races.paceDynamic: Valiant Force will lead from the gates with no early pressure, setting sustainable fractions over this straight 5f trip. Mission Central, Moss Tucker, Ipanema Queen, Lady Iman and Likedbymike will create a congested prominent group, with traffic issues likely developing 2-3 furlongs out as they bunch together. The lack of early pace pressure means the leaders won't stop, while the prominent runners face navigation problems in a tight finish. This setup clearly favours front runners and hold-up horses who can find clear runs, penalising the overcrowded prominent brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Stay Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Valiant Force maintains his lead and the prominent group gets tangled up
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader kicks clear while Mission Central and others struggle for racing room in the congested pack behind. Hold-up horses like Keke and Black Forza benefit from the solid pace and find smoother passages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Sorts
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners can navigate the traffic and produce their kicks
scenarios.body: Mission Central's class tells as Ryan Moore finds a gap, with Lady Iman and Likedbymike also getting clear runs. The sustainable pace allows them to wear down Valiant Force in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint from halfway
scenarios.body: Keke and Black Forza time their runs perfectly from the back as the leaders and prominent group come back to them. The lack of early gallop turns this into a pure speed test favouring the closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses get severely hampered and the race becomes a lottery
scenarios.body: The tight finish creates interference throughout the field with several runners getting blocked or checked. An outsider who avoids trouble or gets a dream run through gaps can capitalise on the mayhem.

watchPoints.text: Watch for severe interference 2f out when Mission Central, Moss Tucker, Lady Iman, Ipanema Queen and Likedbymike converge
Monitor if Valiant Force can sustain his kick having shown poor turf form recently despite leading
Check if Black Forza shows any sharpness after 205-day absence when making his run
Observe whether Keke can handle career-high mark of 104 in Listed company
Note if Lady Iman shows any ring-rustiness after 247-day break when asked for effort
